# 1.2 · Slope Finder

`Level 1: Numbers That Learn` · `+15 XP` · `drill 2 of 3`

## The job
Measure slopes numerically. `derivative(f, x)` estimates f'(x) with a central difference.
`gradient(f, point)` returns every partial derivative of a function of several variables.
`check_gradient(f, grad_f, point)` compares a hand-written gradient against your numeric
one and returns True only when every component agrees.

## Why it matters
Gradient checking is how people debug backpropagation code: when the analytic gradient and
the brute-force one disagree, the analytic one is almost always the liar. You will use this
exact trick to test your autograd engine in level 2.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 1.2     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 1.2      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Central difference: (f(x + h) - f(x - h)) / (2h). It is far more accurate than the one-sided version for the same h.
2. For a partial derivative, nudge one coordinate up and down while holding the others still. Copy the point list before you change it.
3. Compare with relative error, |a - n| / max(1e-8, |a| + |n|), so big and small gradients are judged fairly.

</details>
